$comment: Frozen v1. These bytes never change. An implementation is conformant iff it reproduces every vector here. See WIRE-SPEC.md. Changing an existing vector is a breaking wire change requiring a coordinated cluster upgrade; a new encoding gets a new Version and a NEW vector. The annotation arrays are for human review and are not asserted.

vectors.name: header/v1/max-ints
annotation: 02 08 7fffffffffffffff     INTEGER 2^63-1           PrevSeq (widest INTEGER a signed int64 reaches)

vectors.name: header/v1/seq-127
annotation: 02 01 7f        INTEGER 127              PrevSeq — the last value that fits one content byte

vectors.name: header/v1/seq-128
annotation: 30 2c             SEQUENCE, 44 bytes — one byte longer than seq-127
02 02 00 80     INTEGER 128              PrevSeq — INTEGER is signed, so 0x80 alone would be -128; DER prepends 0x00

vectors.name: proposal/v0/empty
annotation: 04 00           OCTET STRING, 0 bytes    Payload — nil and empty encode identically

vectors.name: proposal/v0/smartbft-reference
annotation: Observed from the unmodified fork: types.Proposal{Payload:"PAY", Header:"HDR", Metadata:"MET", VerificationSequence:7}.
Proposal.Digest() returns exactly the sha256 above. The migrated Digest() must reproduce both.
Wire order is struct DECLARATION order. The keyed literal in the fork's Digest() lists the fields differently; keyed literals do not reorder fields.

vectors.name: proposal/v0/len-128
annotation: 30 81 8a               SEQUENCE, 138 bytes — long length form: 0x81 says one length byte follows
04 81 80 00..7f      OCTET STRING, 128 bytes  Payload — 127 would be short form 04 7f
Long form is minimal: 128 encodes as 81 80, never 82 00 80.

vectors.name: genesis/v1/no-members
annotation: 30 3b                SEQUENCE, 59 bytes — every length here is short form
02 01 04           INTEGER 4                MaxNodes — the ceiling, not the current size
30 00              SEQUENCE OF, 0 bytes     Members — empty; per 2.6 absent and empty are the same bytes

vectors.name: genesis/v1/n4
annotation: A four-node cluster, the smallest that tolerates one Byzantine fault.
30 82 01 5d              SEQUENCE, 349 bytes — past 255, so 82 and two length bytes
30 82 01 20            SEQUENCE OF, 288 bytes   Members, ascending by NodeID
Swapping any two members changes the bytes and therefore the pinned digest; the producer sorts, and an unsorted set is refused rather than sorted.

vectors.name: genesis/v1/long-form-length
annotation: Two members are already enough to push Members past 127 content bytes, which is where the length form changes.
30 81 cc                 SEQUENCE, 204 bytes — 81 says one length byte follows
30 81 90               SEQUENCE OF, 144 bytes   Members — long form; 144 encodes as 81 90, never 82 00 90

vectors.name: sigset/v0/empty
annotation: The empty set is expressible and encodes to four bytes. SmartBFT's CommitSignaturesDigest short-circuits to a nil digest before reaching the encoder, so these bytes are never hashed in practice; the vector pins the outer wrapper so an implementer can see it around a SEQUENCE OF that happens to be empty.

vectors.name: sigset/v0/one-signer
annotation: The sha256 here is the digest SmartBFT produced for this input before the migration to this package; it is the contract the structure exists to reproduce.

vectors.name: sigset/v0/three-signers
annotation: Also a pre-migration SmartBFT digest. Signer 2 carries empty Value and Msg (an absent signature is not distinguishable from an empty one, per 2.6), and signer 300 is the first NodeID needing two INTEGER content bytes. Entry order is the caller's and is preserved, not sorted.

vectors.name: signed/v1/commit
annotation: The envelope named in 3.8. GenesisDigest is the SHA-256 of vector genesis/v1/n4, so this envelope names the cluster the signature is for. It is never transmitted: a verifier reconstructs the envelope with its own genesis digest, which is why a signature minted against another cluster cannot be made to verify.
04 20 6f01…dc56               OCTET STRING, 32 bytes   GenesisDigest (SHA-256 of genesis/v1/n4)
04 07 5041594c4f4144          OCTET STRING "PAYLOAD"   Payload - DER of CommitPayloadV1 in practice, opaque here

vectors.name: signed/v1/opaque
annotation: Byte for byte signed/v1/commit with one content byte changed - 02 01 02 in place of 02 01 01 - and an unrelated digest. This is the view-change / opaque Sign purpose.

vectors.name: signed/v1/client-request
annotation: The client-request purpose over the same payload.

vectors.name: signed/v1/read-index
annotation: The read-index attestation purpose over the same payload. These four vectors carry one payload under all four purposes and hash to four unrelated digests, which is the whole of 3.8.3: a captured commit signature presented as a read-index attestation covers bytes that do not exist.

vectors.name: signed/v1/long-form-length
annotation: A 200-byte payload puts both the payload and the outer SEQUENCE into DER long-form length. Per 2.4 the only legal spellings are 81 c8 and 81 f3; 82 00 c8 must be rejected.
30 81 f3                        SEQUENCE, 243 bytes      long form: 81 says one length byte follows

vectors.name: blob/v1/basic
annotation: A signature travelling beside the payload it covers. Payload is the DER of vector commit-payload/v1/with-aux; Value is 00 01 02 … 3f, a placeholder in signature position.

There is no GenesisDigest field and no signer field. A verifier holding genesis digest 6f01…dc56 - the SHA-256 of vector genesis/v1/n4 - reconstructs the envelope of 3.8 as SignedV1{1, 1, 6f01…dc56, Payload}, whose DER is:

Value is the Ed25519 signature over those 88 envelope bytes. A verifier holding a different genesis digest reconstructs different bytes and the signature fails - it does not fail a field comparison, it fails cryptographically, and there is no field in this vector an attacker could have set.

vectors.name: blob/v1/signed-by-test-key
annotation: The one vector in this annex carrying a real Ed25519 signature. Every other vector records a format; this one records a signature a client can check, which is what turns KV-05's 'verifiable by the client' from a design statement into an executed one - ci/verify_vectors.py executes it in Python, not in the language the cluster is written in.

Signing key: the fixed 32-byte seed 000102030405060708090a0b0c0d0e0f101112131415161718191a1b1c1d1e1f. A conformance vector produced from a random key is one nobody else can regenerate; from this seed anyone reproduces the signature below without this repository. The Ed25519 public key it derives is 03a107bff3ce10be1d70dd18e74bc09967e4d6309ba50d5f1ddc8664125531b8, recorded in fields as PubKey.

PubKey and GenesisDigest are NOT fields of SignedBlobV1 and are not on the wire. 3.9.1 froze the envelope as something the verifier reconstructs from its OWN genesis digest, so there is no field here for an attacker to set; der carries Version, Purpose, Payload and Value and nothing else. Both are recorded as the verifier's inputs, and that distinction is the easiest thing in this annex to misread.
Purpose is 4 and Payload is a ReadIndexV1, so this is the read-index attestation a client actually receives rather than a synthetic blob.
The bytes Value covers, reconstructed per 3.9.1 as SignedV1{1, 4, <verifier's genesis digest>, Payload}:

A verifier holding any other genesis digest reconstructs different bytes, and this signature does not cover them. Flipping one bit of Value breaks it too; both negatives are asserted, in Go by TestSignedVectorVerifies and in Python by ci/negative-gate.sh.
Payload decoded, which is what purpose 4 names in 3.8.5:
04 10 b1*16                 OCTET STRING, 16 bytes   Nonce - client chosen

vectors.name: commit-payload/v1/with-aux
annotation: What a consenter signature covers. ProposalDigest is the SHA-256 of vector proposal/v0/smartbft-reference, so this vector binds to a proposal the annex already pins. Aux is the fork's auxiliary input, relayed verbatim and opaque here.
Both fields sit under one signature, which is what makes a consenter signature non-transplantable: it cannot be lifted onto another proposal, and the aux cannot be swapped by whoever relays it.
04 20 35d8…7522               OCTET STRING, 32 bytes   ProposalDigest (SHA-256 of proposal/v0/smartbft-reference)

vectors.name: commit-payload/v1/empty-aux
annotation: The same proposal with no auxiliary input. Per 2.6 an absent Aux and an empty one are the same 04 00 and cannot be told apart, so a verifier that needs the distinction carries it elsewhere.

vectors.name: client-request/v1/no-intermediates
annotation: The request named in 3.11. It carries its own leaf, so a replica catching up by state transfer verifies it against the genesis CA root alone and reaches the verdict a replica that saw it live reached.
There is no ClientID field. The client's identity is the SPIFFE ID of the verified ClientCert, derived and never asserted.
The chain is absent, which per 3.11.2 is the empty SEQUENCE OF 30 00 and not an omitted field: 2.3 bans OPTIONAL, so absent and empty have one spelling.
04 0b 434c..4146              OCTET STRING, 11 bytes   ClientCert - DER of the client leaf, opaque here
30 00                         SEQUENCE OF, 0 bytes     Intermediates - absent chain
04 10 0001..0e0f              OCTET STRING, 16 bytes   RequestID - exactly RequestIDLen, per 3.11.1
04 07 5041594c4f4144          OCTET STRING "PAYLOAD"   Payload - the application request, opaque here

vectors.name: client-request/v1/one-intermediate
annotation: The same request with one intermediate. Each element is a CertificateV1 SEQUENCE wrapping one DER certificate, because the type profile of 2.2 has no slice of slices.
The chain is ordered leaf-ward to root-ward and the order is inside the signed bytes, so a relay that reorders it destroys the signature.

vectors.name: client-request/v1/long-form-length
annotation: A 200-byte payload, so the Payload OCTET STRING takes the 0x81 long form and the outer SEQUENCE the 0x82 form. Both are pinned here per 2.4; 04 82 00 c8 and 30 81 0b would be non-minimal and MUST be rejected.

vectors.name: read-index/v1/basic
annotation: The attestation named in 3.12, carried as SignedV1.Payload under purpose 4. SignerID is inside the signed bytes, so an attestation cannot be re-attributed by whoever relays it.
The nonce is the client's freshness challenge and is exactly NonceLen bytes; a short one narrows the challenge, which is the whole mechanism.
04 10 a7*16                   OCTET STRING, 16 bytes   Nonce - client chosen

vectors.name: read-index/v1/high-seq
annotation: Seq is 2^32 + 42, past what a 32-bit reader holds. An implementer who parses INTEGER into a 32-bit type fails here rather than silently attesting to sequence 42.

vectors.name: commit-cert/v1/n4-q3
annotation: The certificate named in 3.13: three signatures, the quorum at n=4. It is a container and is not itself signed.

Each Msg is the DER of vector commit-payload/v1/with-aux. A client reconstructs SignedV1{1, 1, its own genesis digest, Msg} and verifies Value over those bytes; the envelope is never transmitted. See 3.9.1.
Sigs is strictly ascending by Signer and rejected otherwise on both encode and decode, so an unsorted certificate has no second spelling. This is 2.2's rule with no exception, unlike 3.7.4.
How many entries a client must require is a property of the cluster size and is specified outside this document.
04 20 35d8..7522              OCTET STRING, 32 bytes   ProposalDigest (SHA-256 of proposal/v0/smartbft-reference)
30 82 01 5f                   SEQUENCE OF, 351 bytes   Sigs, ascending by Signer
04 40 a1*64               OCTET STRING, 64 bytes   Value - Ed25519 over the reconstructed envelope

vectors.name: commit-cert/v1/n13-q9
annotation: The same decision with nine signatures, the quorum at n=13. Same proposal, same view and seq: only the signature set differs, which is what a larger cluster changes about this structure.
30 82 04 1d                   SEQUENCE OF, 1053 bytes  Sigs, signers 1..9 ascending

vectors.name: commit-cert/v1/long-form-length
annotation: One entry whose Msg is 300 bytes, so the Msg OCTET STRING takes the 0x82 two-octet length form. No other vector pins that form on a primitive, and 04 83 00 01 2c would be non-minimal and MUST be rejected per 2.4.

merkle.name: merkle/leaf/tree2
annotation: Same key and value as merkle/leaf/basic, different treeID, different hash: a leaf cannot be relocated across trees.

merkle.name: merkle/leaf/depth1
annotation: Same tree and payload as merkle/leaf/basic, different depth, different hash: a leaf cannot be relocated within a tree.

merkle.name: merkle/internal/basic
annotation: Children are fixed 32-byte digests and carry no length prefix.

merkle.name: merkle/empty/basic
annotation: A third prefix, not a leaf of empty key and empty value: otherwise non-membership and membership-of-empty collide.

merkle.name: merkle/empty/tree2
annotation: An empty subtree is bound to its tree too, so an absence proof from the revision log does not transfer to the key index.
